subject: Request: FinLytics runway sponsorship for 48h POC soak
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics Ops <ops@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: FinLytics runway sponsorship for 48h POC soak

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the platform demo last week — it helped us map the spike behaviour for our recommendation models. We're aiming to run a 48-hour POC soak (latency + throughput validation) to prove SLA headroom before we finalize an internal purchase.

Quick summary:
- Window: Fri Mar 23 22:00 PT -> Sun Mar 25 22:00 PT (48h)
- Target steady concurrency: ~350 RPS (spikes to 1k RPS for short bursts)
- Estimated token consumption: ~12M tokens (in total) across mixed prompts; main model: redwood/rlm-13b-opt (we can run compatible variant you suggest)
- Success metrics: p95 generation latency < 220ms for median prompt length, < 2% error/timeout rate

Can Redwood provision a promotional runway (trial credits / sandbox fuel) for the above window so we can run without billing surprises? Attached is a short POC plan and our load script.

Attachments: finlytics_poc-plan.pdf (7 pages), load-script.tar.gz (script + harness)

Open to a short call if you need more detail — ideally we lock this down today so infra team can schedule.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops
FinLytics
elena@finlytics.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FinLytics runway sponsorship for 48h POC soak

Elena — thanks for the clear outline and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions so I can route for approval: 

1) Which model variant do you plan to use exactly (fp16 vs quantized)? quantized runs make a big difference on token budget.
2) Do you need streaming responses enabled for the test or are you running full-response fetches?
3) Is the 350 RPS steady the client-side request rate or the expected server-side generation throughput (we usually see a 10–15% amplification due to retries/metadata calls)?

I'll loop in Sales Ops and our trial-credit approver once I get those numbers — Monica (cc'd) will stand by for the weekend support window if we approve. If it's easier we can do a 15-min sync at 11:00 PT.

Folks — quick policy note from Sales Ops: sales reps can provision promotional runway up to an equivalent of 20k tokens without manager approval. Anything above that needs manager sign-off and an approval form.

Based on Elena's estimate (~12M tokens) that's well above the self-serve ceiling. Options:
- We can provide a staggered runway: an initial 20k-token promotional allocation immediately to validate the harness, then a manager-approved top-up for the full 48h run; or
- If the customer can scope down the soak (shorter window / lower concurrency), we might fit within the 20k limit for a representative soak.

I'm attaching the approval_form.pdf to capture usage window and ROI metrics if Marissa is comfortable approving a larger one-off. Marissa — tagging you for sign-off. If approved, Sales Ops will create a limited promo credit tied to the HubSpot deal and restrict it to the Fri->Sun window.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Director, Enterprise Sales
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: approval_form.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FinLytics runway sponsorship for 48h POC soak — approval

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the POC plan and FinLytics' usage profile. I'm comfortable approving a one-time promotional runway of 50,000 token-equivalent credits for this 48-hour soak, subject to the following conditions: 

- The promo credit is valid only for the window Fri Mar 23 22:00 PT -> Sun Mar 25 22:00 PT; unused credits will expire immediately after.
- Model variant: limit to quantized-compatible redwood/rlm-13b-opt-q8 for the run (to reduce backend amplification).
- Monica, please standby for on-call support during the window (Monica has the escalation playbook).
- FinLytics will share the POC soak metrics (latency distribution, error rates, and a short post-run summary) within 72 hours after the run. We'll attach the approval record to the HubSpot deal.

I've attached a signed promo_approval_record.pdf and logged the approval on HubSpot (link below). Ben — please create the promo credit and scope it strictly to the deal and window.

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — thank you, this is great news. We'll switch the harness to the q8-compatible path and schedule the run for the approved window. Monica — I'll share a Slack channel and our runbook so you can jump in if anything spikes.

We'll send the post-run summary (latency p50/p95/p99, error breakdown, and a short recommendation) within 48 hours of completion.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will confirm final start time by EOD tomorrow.
